breaking: 🚨 OIL: Brent crude rose to around $101.48 as markets watched for possible diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran at the UN General Assembly.

🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran has reportedly communicated conditions for returning to negotiations, while Donald Trump has indicated he is open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. No new agreement has been confirmed.
🛢️ Saudi Aramco has increased crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, with tanker-tracking data showing about 14 million barrels loaded onto seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday.

🇫🇷🇺🇦🇷🇺 Emmanuel Macron says he discussed with Donald Trump the possibility of a moratorium on attacks against energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia. No Russia–Ukraine energy truce has yet been agreed.
🇨🇦🇪🇺 Canada and the European Union continue discussions over a proposed new associate-member relationship. Canada is not joining the EU.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 Washington and Beijing remain engaged in talks covering trade, tariffs, AI and critical minerals ahead of the Trump–Xi summit.
🇺🇳 World leaders are gathering in New York for the UN General Assembly amid conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, energy-security concerns, trade disputes and debates over AI governance.
🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery is attracting more Nigerian fuel buyers as current import-parity prices for petrol are above the refinery's reported gantry price.
🇳🇬 Aliko Dangote says the group's fertiliser business is planned for a 2028 IPO, with expansion expected to take combined Nigeria and Ethiopia capacity towards about 12 million tonnes annually.

⚠️ Kenya's Capital Markets Authority says the Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO has not been submitted for approval in Kenya. Nigerian investors are subject to the Nigerian offer and regulatory framework.
🇳🇬 Nigeria handled 103,375 imported vehicles in the first half of 2026, a 42.5% increase from the same period in 2025.
🇵🇰🇦🇫 Pakistan says its strikes in the Pakistan–Afghanistan border region killed at least 28 militants. The casualty figure is a Pakistani claim and has not been independently verified.
🇬🇱🇩🇰🇺🇸 Denmark, Greenland and the United States are expected to sign a new security agreement that would significantly expand the US military presence in Greenland.
🛢️ Global diesel prices have reached record levels as conflicts disrupt supplies from major producers including Russia, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

featured.title: Oil Rises as Markets Watch Possible US–Iran Diplomacy
featured.content: Oil prices rose for the first time in five sessions as investors assessed the possibility of diplomatic progress between Washington and Tehran during the United Nations General Assembly. Brent crude rose to about $101.48 per barrel, while October WTI traded around $96.65 and the more actively traded November contract around $93.22. Markets remain highly sensitive to any evidence of negotiations because the Middle East conflict continues to disrupt shipping and energy infrastructure. Saudi Aramco has increased crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, while ship-to-ship transfers near Oman are also helping maintain regional oil flows.

articles.title: US–Iran Diplomacy Comes Into Focus at UN General Assembly
articles.content: Oil markets are watching for signs of renewed US–Iran diplomacy as world leaders gather in New York. Iran has reportedly communicated conditions under which it could return to negotiations, while US President Donald Trump has said he would be willing to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. No agreement has been announced, and the conflict continues to affect regional shipping and energy supplies.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran diplomacy United Nations flags

articles.title: Saudi Aramco Increases Oil Exports Through Hormuz
articles.content: Saudi Arabia is increasing crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz despite continuing security risks. Tanker-tracking data indicated that around 14 million barrels were loaded onto seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday. Middle Eastern producers are also increasingly using ship-to-ship transfers near Oman to maintain exports while conventional routes remain under pressure.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Aramco oil tanker Gulf shipping

articles.title: Macron Discusses Possible Russia–Ukraine Energy Truce With Trump
articles.content: French President Emmanuel Macron says he held a constructive discussion with Donald Trump about the possibility of a moratorium on attacks against energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia. Macron also stressed the need to strengthen Ukraine's air defences and provide additional interceptors. He plans to raise the issue further with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. At present, there is no confirmed energy-sector truce.
articles.imageQuery: Emmanuel Macron Donald Trump Ukraine diplomacy

articles.title: Canada–EU Associate-Member Proposal Remains Under Discussion
articles.content: Canada's proposed closer relationship with the European Union remains a major diplomatic story. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed exploring an associate-member status for Canada, while Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed deeper cooperation. France's Emmanuel Macron has also backed the idea. Canada is not becoming an EU member, and the proposed status has no established EU treaty framework. Any arrangement would require negotiations over its rights, obligations and institutional structure.

articles.title: US–China Relations Remain Central to Global Trade Outlook
articles.content: Washington and Beijing remain engaged in discussions over tariffs, trade, artificial intelligence and critical minerals. The relationship between the world's two largest economies remains crucial to global manufacturing and supply chains. Any major agreement or renewed dispute could affect technology companies, manufacturers, investors and consumers far beyond the two countries.
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump Xi Jinping US China trade

articles.title: UN General Assembly Opens Amid Multiple Global Crises
articles.content: World leaders are gathering in New York for the annual United Nations General Assembly. The meeting comes against the backdrop of the Middle East conflict, the war in Ukraine, disrupted energy markets, international shipping risks, trade disputes, AI governance and humanitarian emergencies. Diplomacy at the UN will be closely watched for signs of progress on several of these issues.
articles.imageQuery: United Nations General Assembly New York leaders

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Gains Advantage as Nigerian Import Costs Rise
articles.content: Oil marketers are increasingly lifting petrol and diesel from the Dangote Petroleum Refinery as estimated import-parity prices rise above the refinery's reported selling price. Punch reports that Dangote's petrol gantry price was ₦1,350 per litre from September 17, compared with an estimated import-parity price of about ₦1,364–₦1,365 per litre on the spot-market benchmark. The development comes as international energy disruption continues to affect fuel markets.

articles.title: Dangote Fertiliser Targets 2028 IPO
articles.content: Aliko Dangote has announced plans to take the Dangote fertiliser business public in 2028. The group expects fertiliser production capacity across Nigeria and a proposed Ethiopian operation to reach about 12 million tonnes annually by then. The planned listing would follow the current Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO and could become another major development for Nigeria's capital market.

articles.title: Kenya Regulator Clarifies Dangote Refinery IPO Status
articles.content: Kenya's Capital Markets Authority has warned investors that the Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO has not been submitted for approval in Kenya. The offer is being conducted under Nigeria's regulatory framework. Investors outside Nigeria should verify any platform claiming to sell authorised Dangote Refinery shares before transferring money.

articles.title: Nigeria Vehicle Imports Rise 42.5% in First Half
articles.content: Nigeria handled 103,375 imported vehicles at its ports between January and June 2026, up 42.5% from 72,568 units during the same period in 2025. Nigerian Ports Authority data also showed 2,152 vessel calls, a 6.9% year-on-year increase, while total cargo throughput reached about 68.29 million metric tonnes, up 12.2%. The port figures point to stronger activity across several areas of Nigeria's maritime sector.

articles.title: Pakistan Reports 28 Militants Killed in Border Strikes
articles.content: Pakistan says military strikes in the Pakistan–Afghanistan border region killed at least 28 militants. The reported casualties come amid continuing tensions between Islamabad and armed groups operating around the border. The figure has been provided by Pakistani authorities and should be treated as a reported claim until independently verified.

articles.title: Houthi Activity Keeps Red Sea Shipping Under Pressure
articles.content: Security concerns remain elevated around Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a major maritime route connecting the Indian Ocean with the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal. Continued Houthi activity has contributed to shipping companies rerouting vessels, increasing voyage times, fuel consumption and insurance costs.
articles.imageQuery: Bab el Mandeb Red Sea cargo ship Yemen

articles.title: US Plans Expanded Military Presence in Greenland
articles.content: Denmark, Greenland and the United States are expected to sign a new security arrangement during the UN General Assembly. Reuters reports that the United States plans to reopen a former Cold War-era military site at Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland and establish another military presence at Mestersvig in eastern Greenland. Denmark has said Greenland's sovereignty will not be compromised. The arrangement is linked to NATO and the growing strategic importance of the Arctic.
articles.imageQuery: Greenland Arctic US Denmark military base

articles.title: Global Diesel Prices Reach Record Levels
articles.content: Global diesel markets remain under severe pressure as conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine disrupt supplies from major producers. Reuters reports that European diesel futures have risen to more than twice their level at the start of 2026, while US retail diesel prices have exceeded $6 per gallon for the first time. Refiners are operating at high utilisation rates, leaving limited spare capacity to quickly replace lost supply.
articles.imageQuery: diesel fuel pump Europe energy crisis

articles.title: Asian Markets Rise as Oil Prices Ease and Diplomacy Offers Hope
articles.content: Asian shares advanced on Tuesday as investors responded to lower recent oil prices and hopes for progress in US–Iran diplomacy. Technology stocks also gained, while markets continued to monitor US interest-rate expectations, currency movements and the upcoming Trump–Xi summit. The improvement in sentiment remains sensitive to developments in the Middle East.

morningSummary: Good morning. Oil markets are beginning Tuesday with renewed attention on possible US–Iran diplomacy at the United Nations, while the wider Middle East conflict continues to disrupt shipping and fuel markets. Brent crude has moved back above $101 as investors assess whether negotiations could reduce the risk of further supply disruption. In Europe, Emmanuel Macron says he discussed a possible moratorium on attacks against Russian and Ukrainian energy infrastructure with Donald Trump. Canada and the EU continue discussions over a proposed associate-member relationship, while the UN General Assembly brings world leaders together in New York. In Nigeria, the Dangote Refinery is gaining additional demand as imported fuel becomes more expensive, while Dangote Fertiliser is targeting a potential 2028 IPO. Nigeria's vehicle imports also rose sharply during the first half of the year.
